parsed.explanation: Worst documented feature is tier-1 state-imposed universal exposure: the February 2026 law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in all publicly owned buildings — explicitly including airports — with civil and criminal penalties and a private bounty mechanism that lets any person sue, so enforcement does not depend on an agency or prosecutor. Existing licences whose markers mismatch are invalidated at the holder's expense, and a trans-focused assessment moved the division to 'Do Not Travel'. On top sits the parent regime: passport/visa marker restrictions with documented confiscation and stranding, an entry cable inviting lifetime fraud ineligibility findings, and documented custodial harm (forced labour, sexual abuse in immigration custody). Mitigating but not offsetting: no general presentation offence, a 2020 public-accommodations law, functioning courts, and a pending challenge — none of which restrains the bounty or ID rules. Rated materially below the parent average.
